newsitem.title: USA: New York mayor seeks limit on some bonds - NYT.
newsitem.headline: New York mayor seeks limit on some bonds - NYT.

text.p: New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani wants to scale back the growing influence of the city's business improvement districts by limiting or ending their ability to sell bonds, The New York Times reported on Thursday.
The proposed restrictions would make it difficult for the districts to undertake multimillion-dollar projects.

The mayor believes the city has too little control over the districts' finances and would be held responsible if any defaulted on their debt, administration officials said. A default might damage New York's already shaky credit rating.
Giuliani has not formally decided to restrict the districts' authority to borrow money through bond sales but probably will do so.
"I certainly think that we are moving in that direction," said Fran Relter, the deputy mayor for economic development.
The city has more than 30 business districts. They levy special taxes on property owners and use the money to pick up garbage, hire security guards, promote businesses and carry out other activities.
Two of the most prominent districts, the Grand Central Partnership and the 34th Street Partnership, have sold a total of $56.5 million in bonds in recent years.
The Grand Central Partnership recently asked the Giuliani administration to approve another $10.7 million in bond sales so it can help the city renovate Grand Central Terminal.
